article_title: Conjuring Power from a Theory of Change: The PWRD Method for Trials with Anticipated Variation in Effects
citation: Timothy Lycurgus, Ben B. Hansen, and Mark White. (2022). Conjuring Power from a Theory of Change: The PWRD Method for Trials with Anticipated Variation in Effects. Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness. https://doi.org/10.1080/19345747.2022.2142178
title: PWRD aggregation: a method converting an intervention's theory of change into power-maximizing weights for aggregating cohort-year ITT effect estimates
description: PWRD (power-maximizing weighting for repeated measurements with delayed effects) aggregation is a statistical scheme for randomized trials and quasi-experiments with longitudinal data. It computes separate ITT effect estimates for each cohort-year of follow-up and combines them with weights proportional to expected effect size and estimate precision: "the 'signal-to-noise' ratio of test statistics centered around ^Dagg will be maximized by weights proportional both to the expected sizes of cohort-year effects, p, and also to the relative precisions of estimated cohort-year effects, R". Expected effect sizes come from the proportion of students eligible for supplemental instruction, derived from the intervention's theory of change. The method maintains the intention-to-treat perspective and is designed for hypothesis testing, usable alongside standard estimation.
requirements: Requires baseline or post-treatment measures of intervention delivery or availability, in combination with primary outcomes measured on varying numbers of occasions
Requires a robust and well-articulated theory of change identifying which observations are likely to manifest a treatment effect
Requires estimates of eligibility proportions (p) and relative covariances (R) to formulate the aggregation weights
constraints: Conditions 2.1 and 2.2 (effects proportional to share non-excluded, effects retained) are not required for validity of the hypothesis test but are necessary for finding an efficient estimator
No benefit is gained when the supporting theory of change is incorrect
target_learners: Researchers analyzing education RCTs and quasi-experiments with longitudinal outcome data
target_learning_goals: Detecting effects of supplemental-instruction interventions with delayed, non-uniform effects
examples: In the BURST evaluation, weights for Cohort 1.K were (0.25, 0, 0.32, 0.43) across the four follow-up years, with zero weight on year 2 due to its relative imprecision
